lines.speaker: e
lines.text: One steamship stopped miles from the sinking Titanic, watched eight white rockets, and never moved to help.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: On April fourteenth, nineteen twelve, Captain Stanley Lord stopped the steamer Californian at an Atlantic ice field. Her lone radio operator switched off his set and went to bed.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: After midnight, Second Officer Herbert Stone watched a nearby steamer fire white rockets, eight in all. He said a ship does not fire rockets at sea for nothing.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Yet Captain Lord told his men to keep using the Morse lamp. The radio stayed off until after four-thirty, when the Titanic had already sunk.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The British inquiry said the Californian might have saved many, if not all, of the lives lost.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Lord claimed a smaller third ship fired the rockets. A U S Navy hydrographer found no third ship in the area.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: So why did one steamship watch eight rockets, and never wake its radio operator?
